title: International Space Station Pass Reminder
dataSources: Seismograph (`seismo:reading`), Geiger counter (`geiger:cpm`), lightning strikes (`lightning:strike`), radon (`radon:reading`), all-sky meteor camera (`allsky:capture`), river-level gauge (`riverlevel:reading`), magnetometer (`magnetometer:reading`).
app: DIY citizen-science sensors — Raspberry Shake seismograph, DIY Geiger counter, AS3935/Blitzortung lightning detector, radon monitor, all-sky meteor camera, river-level gauge, and magnetometer — streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=satpass:prediction satellite=ISS
| eval mins_away=round((pass_epoch-now())/60,0)
| where mins_away>0 AND mins_away<60 AND max_elevation>30
| sort mins_away
| table pass_epoch mins_away max_elevation direction
description: Reminds you when the Space Station will make a bright, high pass over your location so you can catch it with the naked eye.
value: The ISS is easy to see but easy to miss; a timely reminder for the good high passes turns a rare glimpse into a regular treat.
implementation: Ingest ISS pass predictions into `index=personal`; alert shortly before a high-elevation evening pass.
visualization: Table of upcoming ISS passes with time, elevation, and direction.
grandmaExplanation: It reminds you just before the Space Station flies over so you can go outside and watch it cross the sky.
